en: The Abstederbrug is a national monument bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The stone arched bridge is located on the southeast side of the Utrecht city center and spans the Tolsteeg/Maliesingel. The bridge dating from 1901 has two spans and was designed by the Department of Municipal Works under the direction of F.J. Nieuwenhuis.

en: The Admiralengracht is a canal and street name in Amsterdam-West, the canal was dug in the 1920s as part of the Plan West. The canal was named in 1924, after the Dutch and Zeelandish admirals from the 16th, 17th, 18th and 19th centuries, after which many streets in the surrounding district, the Admiralenbuurt, are named.

name: Afrikahaven
en: The Afrikahaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area. The port was dug in 1997-2001 and is located on the south side of the North Sea Canal, in the Houtrakpolder, west of the former Zijkanaal F.

name: Afrikahuis
en: The Afrikahuis is the former church of the Roman Catholic Sint Willibrordus parish in the De Pijp district of Amsterdam. The municipal monument has not been used as a place of worship since 2008, but is still owned by the diocese of Haarlem-Amsterdam. Since 2008 it has been used by temporary tenants.

name: Albardagracht

name: Albert
en: Police dog Albert is a small monument from 1924 in the Oosterpark in Amsterdam, consisting of a granite gravestone on a stone plinth. It commemorates the police dog Albert, called Ab or Appie, who lived from 1916 until March 1923. He was the private tracker dog, a Tervuren shepherd, of officer Water.

name: Albert Helmanbrug
en: The Albert Helmanbrug (bridge 1231) is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The bridge connects the Anton de Komplein with the Nelson Mandelapark. Immediately south of it stands the statue of Steve van Dorpel by Nelson Carrilho, which is also the start and finish of a 2.1 km fitness trail through the park.

name: Aldo van Eyckbrug
en: Aldo van Eyckbrug (bridge 413) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid. The four-lane traffic bridge, with cycle and foot paths on both sides and tram line 24 running over it, carries the Amstelveenseweg across the Zuider Amstelkanaal where it becomes the Stadiongracht. The Stadionplein lies at its north-east end.

name: Aldo van Eyckbrug
en: Aldo van Eyckbrug (bridge 413) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid. The four-lane traffic bridge with bicycle and pedestrian paths on both sides, over which tram line 24 also runs, is located on Amstelveenseweg. It spans the Zuider Amstel Canal here, where it flows into the Stadiongracht. On the northeast side of the bridge is Stadionplein.

name: Aluminiumbrug

name: Amerikahaven

name: Annick van Hardeveld

Taking the form of a bluestone plinth with a plaque, it stands on the Hekelveld in front of the building numbered 25, at the point between the Spuistraat and the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. It was designed by the artist Hans Bayens.

name: ASC SDW

name: Beethovenstraat

After the corona crisis, more and more trendy restaurants and bars opened up. Among others, Heemskerk, Purmerend and Zaandam also have a Beethovenstraat.

name: Bella Vistapark
en: The Bella Vistapark is a city park in Amstelkwartier-Noord, Amsterdam-Oost. It is also the name of the footpath through the park. The park, which had existed for some time as part of Park Somerlust, received its name on June 4, 2019 and was named after a country house on the Amstel. The park extends along the inlet harbor with the Zuidergasfabri

name: Bellamyplein
en: The Bellamyplein is a triangular square in the Bellamy neighborhood in Amsterdam-West, between the Bilderdijkkade and the Ten Katestraat. Streets that end on the square are the Kwakersstraat, Elisabeth Wolffstraat, Agatha Dekenstraat, Jan Hanzenstraat and Bellamystraat. At the southern end of the park are two giant trees (tree numbers 504239 and 504235, not

name: Bellevue
en: Theater Bellevue is a theater with three rooms on Leidsekade in Amsterdam.

name: Beltbrug
en: The Beltbrug (bridge 324) is a bridge in Amsterdam-West The traffic bridge connects the Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat with the Jan van Galenstraat in the s105 and spans the Kostverlorenvaart. From the bridge, sawmill De Otter is clearly visible. Just northwest of the bridge is the Buysbrug, a pedestrian and bicycle bridge.

name: Beltbrug
en: The Beltbrug (bridge 324) is a bridge in Amsterdam-West. The traffic bridge connects the Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat with the Jan van Galenstraat on the s105 and spans the Kostverlorenvaart. The De Otter sawmill is clearly visible from the bridge. Just to its north-west lies the Buysbrug, for pedestrians and cyclists.

name: Berekuil
en: A bear pit is a roundabout where the road is raised for vehicular traffic and cyclists are guided through the 'pit' in the middle of the roundabout via bike lanes. The construction is named after the bear pit that was used to catch and keep bears.

name: Berensluis
en: Berensluis (bridge 65) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It forms the connection between Berenstraat and Elandsgracht, crossing the Prinsengracht in the process. In the immediate vicinity was bridge 104 on the quay of the Prinsengracht over the Elandsgracht, the bridge was removed after the latter was dammed. Both bridges can be found on the map

name: Berensluis
en: Berensluis (bridge 65) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Berenstraat with the Elandsgracht, spanning the Prinsengracht. Bridge 104 lay close by in the quay of the Prinsengracht over the Elandsgracht, and was cleared away after that canal was filled in.

name: Berta de Vriesbrug
en: Berta de Vriesbrug (bridge 128) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge, over which no public transport runs, connects Westerstraat with Marnixplein and spans the Lijnbaansgracht.

name: Berta de Vriesbrug
en: Berta de Vriesbrug (bridge 128) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge, which carries no public transport, connects the Westerstraat with the Marnixplein and spans the Lijnbaansgracht. Several municipal monuments stand around it.

name: Bethelkerk
en: The Bethelkerk is a church building in the Dutch city of Utrecht, in the Zuilen district. The church is prominently located on Burgemeester Norbruislaan (house number 1). As a Reformed church, it was built around 1955 according to the design of the architect B.W. Plooij.

name: Betonsluis
en: Sluis 124, also known as the Concrete Lock, is a sluice lock in the IJburg district of Amsterdam. Bridge 2050 crosses the lock.

name: Beudekerbrug
en: The Beudekerbrug (bridge 122) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the north-eastern quay of the Prinsengracht and spans the Leidsegracht in Amsterdam's canal ring. With the Angenietje Swarthofbrug and the Pieter Goemansbrug it forms a crossing over the Leidsegracht and Prinsengracht, surrounded by national monuments.

name: Beudekerbrug
en: The Beudekerbrug (bridge 122) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located on the northeastern quay of the Prinsengracht. It spans the Leidsegracht in the canal belt of Amsterdam. The bridge forms a junction over the Leidse and Prinsengracht with the Angenietje Swarthof Bridge and the Pieter Goemans Bridge.

name: Beulingsloot
en: The Beulingsloot is one of the oldest and shortest canals in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located within the Canal Ring.

name: Beursplein
en: The Beursplein is a square in the center of Amsterdam, between the Damrak and the Beursstraat. On the square are the Effectenbeurs (Beursplein 5), the Beurs van Berlage and the Bijenkorf. On the square is also the entrance to the Bijenkorf parking garage, which regularly causes traffic jams up to the Damrak.

name: Bevrijdingslinde
en: The Bevrijdingslinde van de Jordaankinderen is a war memorial in Amsterdam-Centrum. On 4 May 1946 a lime tree was planted in a garden on the Marnixplein, south of bridge 128 on the western side of the Lijnbaansgracht, in memory of children from the Jordaan, the district on the other side of that canal.

name: Bevrijdingslinde
en: Bevrijdingslinde van de Jordaankinderen is a war monument in Amsterdam-Centrum. On May 4, 1946, a linden tree was planted in a park on Marnixplein south of bridge 128 on the western side of the Lijnbaansgracht. The liberation linden tree was planted in memory of children in the Jordaan (the district is on the other side of the Lijnbaansgracht),

name: Bezembrug
en: The Bezembrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the city center of Utrecht. The bridge spans the Oudegracht.

name: Bijleveldschesluis
en: The Bijleveldschesluis (bridge 495) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum. The original lock has been mostly underground for centuries; it was converted into a one-meter-long tunnel, which runs from the Geldersekade to the Kloveniersburgwal. This means that it runs under the Nieuwmarkt and also the southeastern part of the histori

name: Bijlmerdreef
en: The Bijlmerdreef is the first and also the most important promenade in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Southeast.

name: Bijlmermonument
en: The growing monument (Bijlmer disaster) or Bijlmermonument is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. On October 4 every year, the Bijlmer disaster is commemorated at the monument. Until 2023, a separate "Stichting Beheer Het Groeiend Monument" was responsible for the monument. Since then, the joint neighborhood residents have been responsible.

name: Bijlmerweide
en: The Bijlmerweide is a park in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The park is located east of the low-rise neighborhoods Kantershof and Geerdinkhof, west of the Gaasp river and the Diemerpark, north of the Gaasperpark and Gaasperplas and south of the Verrijn Stuartweg industrial area in Diemen. The Veeneikbrug, a bicycle and pedestrian bridge, connects the Bij

name: Bijltjespad
en: The Bijltjespad is a dead-end car-free side street of the Kattenburgerstraat on the Kattenburg island in the Oostelijke Eilanden district in Amsterdam. On the other side of the Bijltjespad is a student complex. The houses on the other side belong to the Kattenburgerhof. The street name is derived from Bijltjes, a nickname for the in the verle

name: Bijzondere Collecties
en: The Bijzondere Collecties of the University of Amsterdam are part of the university library. They hold the university's heritage, such as rare and valuable books, manuscripts, prints and drawings, photographs, archives, scientific instruments and paintings.

name: Bijzondere Collecties
en: The Bijzondere Collecties of the University of Amsterdam is part of the University Library of Amsterdam. The Bijzondere Collecties houses the heritage of the University of Amsterdam, such as rare and valuable books, manuscripts, prints and drawings, photographs, archives, scientific instruments and paintings. ME

name: Bilderdijkgracht
en: The Bilderdijkgracht is a canal in Amsterdam-West, named after poet and historian Willem Bilderdijk. The canal connects the Hugo de Grootgracht/Kostverlorenvaart at Bilderdijkpark in the north with the Jacob van Lennepkanaal in the south. The canal is crossed by De Clercqstraat (bridge no. 135), Kwakersstraat/Kwakersplein (bridge no.

name: Bilderdijkpark
en: Bilderdijkpark is both a small park and a street in Amsterdam-West. Both were named on April 3, 1912 by council decision after the Dutch author, poet, historian, writer of history, linguist and lawyer Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831).

name: Biltsche Grift
en: The Biltsche Grift is a waterway in the Dutch province of Utrecht. It runs over a distance of roughly 10 kilometers from Zeist to the town of Utrecht located to the west of it. The eastern part from Oostbroek (no. 5 on the large map below) is also referred to as the Zeister Grift. In a broader sense, a now abolished water board was in he

name: Biltstraat
en: The Biltstraat is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht, which separates the neighborhoods Noordoost and Oost. The Biltstraat runs almost straight east and is a little more than a kilometer long.

name: Binnen Dommersstraat
en: Bridge 148 is a lift bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Bisschopswetering
en: Bisschopswetering is a hamlet in the municipality of Kampen in the Dutch province of Overijssel. It is located in the middle of Polder Mastenbroek north of the IJssel.

name: Blauwkapelseweg
en: The Blauwkapelseweg is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht in the district de Wittevrouwen, which runs from the roundabout with the Kardinaal de Jongweg, Eykmanlaan, Van Esveldstraat and the Pieter Nieuwlandstraat on it to the Kleine Singel, Gildstraat and Kapelstraat where it merges into it.

name: Bloemgracht
en: The Bloemgracht is a canal in the Jordaan in Amsterdam. The canal connects the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht and runs between and parallel to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and the Bloemstraat. The canal is crossed by the Eerste, Tweede and Derde Leliedwarsstraat.

name: Boerenwetering
en: The Boerenwetering is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Boerenwetering runs from the Singelgracht along the Hobbemakade / Ruysdaelkade southwards and ends in a rectangular pond between Beatrixpark and the RAI.

name: Boerenweteringbrug
en: The Boerenweteringbrug (bridge 406) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Boomkerk
en: De Boom, or Boomkerk, is the usual name for the Roman Catholic Church of St Francis of Assisi in Amsterdam Bos en Lommer. The building has been on the national monuments register since 2005, and the accompanying presbytery is on the municipal monuments list.

name: Bos en Lommerweg
en: The Bos en Lommerweg is a street in Amsterdam-West. The Bos en Lommerweg runs from the Haarlemmerweg to the dike of the Ringspoorbaan. The street is crossed by the Willem de Zwijgerlaan, Admiraal de Ruijterweg and Hoofdweg. Along the extension of the street lies the Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan beyond the dike of the Ringspoorbaan.

name: Botanische Tuinen Universiteit Utrecht
en: The Botanische garden Fort Hoofddijk in Utrecht is a botanical garden of the Botanische Tuinen of the faculty of science of the Universiteit Utrecht. The garden is located on and around Fort Hoofddijk and houses the university's living plant collection. The garden is located on the edge of the Utrecht Science Park university complex (formerly 'De Uith

name: Boy Edgarbrug
en: The Boy Edgarbrug (bridge 1064) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. This fixed bridge dating back to around 1969 comes in the form of a viaduct or tunnel, depending on the point of view. Motorized traffic travels above the span on the Hoogoorddreef; a continuous route for fast traffic. In the tunnel is an offshoot of the Bijlme

name: Boy Edgarbrug
en: The Boy Edgarbrug (bridge 1064) is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. This fixed bridge from around 1969 takes the form of a viaduct or a tunnel, depending on the point of view. Motorised traffic on the Hoogoorddreef, a through route for fast traffic, passes over the span, while an offshoot of the Bijlmerplein runs through the tunnel.

name: Brantasgracht
en: The Brantasgracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

name: Breedstraat
en: The Breedstraat is a street in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. The approximately 250-meter-long street is located between the Wijde Begijnestraat and the Jacobijnenstraat, where it transitions. There is also the Predikherenstraat, which crosses both of these streets.

name: Brigittenbrug
en: The Brigittenbrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the city center of Utrecht. The bridge has a span and spans the Nieuwegracht at the level of the Brigittenstraat. In the landheads there are bridge basements and on the bridge border yards, a stone yard staircase and yard basements.

name: Brouwersgracht
en: The Brouwersgracht is an Amsterdam canal that connects the Singel with the Singelgracht. The canal marks the northwestern border of the canal belt. Between the Prinsengracht and the Singelgracht, the Brouwersgracht forms the northern border of the Jordaan.

name: Brug 11
en: Brug 11 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the western quay of the Singel and spans the Blauwburgwal. The arched bridge is in direct contact along the bank with bridge 10, the Lijnbaansbrug, over that same Singel. Both bridges have been here for centuries; Pieter Bast drew them both on his 1599 map of the city.

name: Brug 11
en: Brug 11 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located on the western quay of the Singel and spans the Blauwburgwal. The vaulted bridge is in direct contact with bridge 10, the Lijnbaansbrug, over the same Singel via the promenade. Both bridges 10 and 11 have been there for centuries. Pieter Bast drew both of them in his plan of the city from 1

name: Brug 117
en: Brug 117 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the Rozengracht and spans the Lijnbaansgracht. There was a bridge here for a long time, slightly further south than where it has stood since 1885, with an abutment between the Rozengracht and Rozenstraat and the De Victor mill on the far side.

name: Brug 117
en: Brug 117 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located in the Rozengracht and spans the Lijnbaansgracht. There had been a bridge here for a long time slightly south of where it is located since 1885.

name: Brug 118
en: Brug 118 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the northern quay of the Bloemgracht. It spans the Lijnbaansgracht and leads to the Marnixstraat. Within walking distance are bridges 119 and the Bullebak sluice, both over the Bloemgracht.

name: Brug 118
en: Brug 118 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the northern quay of the Bloemgracht, spans the Lijnbaansgracht and leads to the Marnixstraat. A stone's throw away lie bridge 119 and the Bullebakssluis, both over the Bloemgracht. A bridge has been here for centuries; it is already drawn on Joan Blaeu's map of 1649.

name: Brug 119
en: Brug 119 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Bloemgracht. Three bridges meet at this crossing of canals: this one, bridge 118 over the Lijnbaansgracht, and the Bullebakssluis over the extended Bloemgracht.

name: Brug 119
en: Brug 119 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located on the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Bloemgracht. At this intersection of canals there are three bridges, this bridge, bridge 118 (over the Lijnbaansgracht) and the Bullebak sluice over the extended Bloemgracht.

name: Brug 126
en: Brug 126 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Egelantiersgracht in the Jordaan in Amsterdam. The bridge connects the Tweede Leliedwarsstraat with the Derde Egelantiersdwarsstraat. There is probably already a bridge here since the construction of the canal.

name: Brug 126
en: Brug 126 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Egelantiersgracht in the Jordaan, connecting the Tweede Leliedwarsstraat with the Derde Egelantiersdwarsstraat. There has probably been a bridge here since the canal was dug. The present bridge dates from 1921, to a design by the Publieke Werken.

name: Brug 127
en: Brug 127 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Brug 142
en: Brug 142 is a pick-up bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge forms the connection between Willemsstraat and Nieuwe Willemsstraat. It spans the Lijnbaansgracht. In 1882, a wooden emergency bridge was built here, as the local connection across the Lijnbaansgracht at the level of Palmstraat was demolished. It was not until 1887 that a tender was made.

name: Brug 142
en: Brug 142 is a drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Willemsstraat with the Nieuwe Willemsstraat, spanning the Lijnbaansgracht. A temporary wooden bridge was placed here in 1882, after the local crossing of the Lijnbaansgracht at the Palmstraat was demolished; a tender for a permanent bridge followed only in 1887.

name: Brug 15
en: Brug 15 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the western quay of the Singel and spans the Brouwersgracht. It is therefore the first bridge over the Brouwersgracht, which you pass towards the city. The bridge is located over the narrowest part of that canal and is barely 10 meters wide and long.

name: Brug 15
en: Brug 15 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the western quay of the Singel and spans the Brouwersgracht, making it the first bridge over the Brouwersgracht coming out of the city. It crosses the narrowest part of that canal and is barely 10 metres wide and long. The much larger Haarlemmersluis lies around the corner.

name: Brug 19
en: Brug 19 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the eastern quay of the Herengracht and spans the Blauwburgwal. It forms a whole with bridge 18, in the southern quay of the Blauwburgwal over the Herengracht. It is surrounded by municipal and national monuments but is not one itself: it is too young.

name: Brug 19
en: Brug 19 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located in the eastern frame of the Herengracht and spans the Blauwburgwal. The bridge forms a whole with bridge 18 in the southern embankment of the Blauwburgwal and over the Herengracht.

name: Brug 21
en: Brug 21 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the western quay of the Herengracht and spans the Leliegracht. The bridge forms a whole with the Anton Joling Bridge (bridge 20), which crosses the Herengracht at a 90-degree angle. There has been a bridge here for centuries. Balthasar Florisz.

name: Brug 21
en: Brug 21 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the western quay of the Herengracht and spans the Leliegracht. It forms a whole with the Anton Jolingbrug (bridge 20), which crosses the Herengracht at a right angle to it. A bridge has been here for centuries; Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode drew one on his map of 1625.

name: Brug 24
en: Brug 24 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Gasthuismolensteeg with the Hartenstraat, spanning the Herengracht. The bridge, not a monument itself, is surrounded by municipal and national monuments. A bridge has been here for centuries: Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode drew one on his map of 1625.

name: Brug 24
en: Brug 24 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It forms the connection between Gasthuismolensteeg and Hartenstraat. It spans the Herengracht. The bridge, itself not a monument, is surrounded by municipal and national monuments. There has been a bridge here for centuries. Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode drew the bridge on his map from 1625, a bridge over

name: Brug 331
en: Brug 331 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-West over a cooling-water channel. Bridge 391, a railway bridge, lies about 10 metres to its north. Twenty metres further on lies the pairing of bridge 330 (road) and bridge 390 (rail) carrying the Nieuwe Hemweg over the same channel.

name: Brug 361
en: Brug 244 is a fixed bridge in Westpoort. The structure lies in the Nieuwe Hemweg and crosses the Tweede Koelwaterkanaal of the Centrale Hemweg. It was designed at the same time as bridge 361 further along the Nieuwe Hemweg, which is why the two look the same. It carries a two-lane road for fast traffic and a two-lane cycle path.

name: Brug 38
en: Brug 38 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Brug 388
en: Brug 275 is a fixed railway bridge in Westpoort, Amsterdam. The bridge with a single track crosses the mouth of the Second Cool Water Canal into the Central Hemweg. It dates from the mid-seventies and was designed by Sier van Rhijn, later responsible for buildings etc. of the Amsterdam metro East Line. The bridge consists of a concrete

name: Brug 388
en: Brug 275 is a fixed railway bridge in Westpoort, Amsterdam. The single-track bridge crosses the mouth of the Tweede Koelwaterkanaal at the Centrale Hemweg. It dates from the mid-1970s and was designed by Sier van Rhijn, later responsible for the buildings of the Amsterdam metro's Oostlijn. The bridge has a concrete span.

name: Brug 39
en: Brug 39 is a bridge in the northern quay of the Keizersgracht over the Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam's canal ring. It has a navigable opening 6.80 metres wide with a clearance of 2.38 metres. There were several plans to fill in the Reguliersgracht, but none were ever carried out.

name: Brug 39
en: Brug 39 is a bridge in the northern quay of the Keizersgracht over the Reguliersgracht in the Amsterdam canal belt. The bridge has a passage opening of 6.80 meters wide and with a passage height of 2.38 meters. There have been several plans to dampen the Reguliersgracht, but these were ultimately never carried out. This vault bridge

name: Brug 390
en: Brug 390 is a fixed bridge in Westpoort, Amsterdam. It is a railway bridge laid over the cooling-water channel of the Centrale Hemweg, parallel to the road bridges numbered 330. Like bridge 330 it has three openings, but shipping of any kind is impossible here: the current is strong and the bridges lie low.

name: Brug 390
en: Brug 390 is a permanent bridge in Westpoort, Amsterdam. It is a railway bridge that was built over the cooling water canal of the Centrale Hemweg. It lies parallel to the traffic bridges numbered 330. Like bridge 330, the railway bridge has three passages, but shipping of any kind is impossible here. There is a strong current and the bridges are low

name: Brug 40
en: Brug 40 is a bridge in the southern quay of the Keizersgracht over the Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam's canal ring. It has a navigable opening 6.80 metres wide with a clearance of 2.38 metres. There were several plans to fill in the Reguliersgracht, but none were ever carried out.

name: Brug 40
en: Brug 40 is a bridge in the southern quay of the Keizersgracht over the Reguliersgracht in the Amsterdam canal belt. The bridge has a passage opening of 6.80 meters wide and with a passage height of 2.38 meters. There have been several plans to dampen the Reguliersgracht, but these were ultimately never carried out. This vaulted bridge

name: Brug 42
en: Brug 42 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat and spans the Keizersgracht. The bridge, not a monument itself, is surrounded by national monuments. A bridge has been here for centuries: city architect Daniël Stalpaert already drew one on the design part of his 1662 map.

name: Brug 42
en: Brug 42 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located in the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat and spans the Keizersgracht. The bridge, itself not a monument, is surrounded by national monuments. There has been a bridge here for centuries.

name: Brug 43
en: Brug 43 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge, over which trams 2 and 12 run in particular, is located in Leidsestraat and spans the Keizersgracht in the Amsterdam Canal Belt. There has been a bridge here for centuries.

name: Brug 43
en: Brug 43 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge, carrying tram lines 2 and 12 in particular, lies in the Leidsestraat and spans the Keizersgracht in Amsterdam's canal ring. A bridge has been here for centuries: city architect Daniël Stalpaert already drew it on his map of 1662.

name: Brug 46
en: Brug 46 (formerly Quellijn bridge) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum The bridge is located on the northern quay of the Leidsegracht and spans the Keizersgracht. Surrounding the bridge are buildings on all eight quays that have been designated as national monuments. The bridge itself could not be declared a monument, it is too young for that.

name: Brug 46
en: Brug 46, formerly the Quellijn brug, is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the northern quay of the Leidsegracht and spans the Keizersgracht. Buildings on all eight quays around the bridge are national monuments. The bridge itself could not be listed: it is too young for that.

name: Brug 47
en: Brug 47 is a welfare bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge connects Huidenstraat with Runstraat and crosses the Keizersgracht in the area of the Nine Streets in the Amsterdam canal belt. The bridge, due to its young age itself no monuments, is surrounded by national monuments, except on the southeast side, there is (relatively) new construction

name: Brug 47
en: Brug 47 is an arched bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Huidenstraat with the Runstraat, crossing the Keizersgracht in the Negen Straatjes area of Amsterdam's canal ring. Too young to be a monument itself, it is surrounded by national monuments except on the south-east side, where the building is relatively new.

name: Brug 51
en: Brug 51 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Brug 52
en: Brug 52 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the western quay of the Keizersgracht and spans the Leliegracht. Seen from the centre, the Leliesluis lies just beyond it. It is flanked by bridges 51, beside it, and 53, on the far side of the Keizersgracht.

name: Brug 52
en: Brug 52 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located on the western quay of the Keizersgracht and spans the Leliegracht. From the center viewed, the Leliesluis is located just behind this bridge. It is flanked by the bridges 51 (next to it) and 53 (across the Keizersgracht).

name: Brug 53
en: Brug 53 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the eastern quay of the Keizersgracht and spans the Leliegracht. It is flanked by bridges 51, beside it, and 52, on the far side of the Keizersgracht. Too young to be a monument itself, it is surrounded by national monuments.

name: Brug 53
en: Brug 53 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located on the eastern quay of the Keizersgracht and spans the Leliegracht. It is flanked by bridges 51 (next to it) and 52 (across the Keizersgracht). The bridge, itself not a monument (it is too young for that), is surrounded by national monuments.

name: Brug 56
en: Brug 56 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge connects the eastern quay of the Keizersgracht with the Binnen Brouwersstraat, crossing the Brouwersgracht. A municipal monument since 1995, it is surrounded by national monuments and shares its south-western quay wall with the Pastoorsbrug.

name: Brug 56
en: Brug 56 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge connects the eastern quay of the Keizersgracht with the Binnen Brouwersstraat. It crosses the Brouwersgracht. The bridge, a municipal monument since 1995, is surrounded by national monuments. The bridge shares its southwest quay wall with the Pastoorsbrug.

name: Brug 6
en: Brug 6 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge connects the Paleisstraat with the Gasthuismolensteeg, spanning the Singel. The Bungehuis stands to its south-east.

name: Brug 66
en: Brug 66 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in line with the Runstraat, heading out of the city, and crosses the Prinsengracht. Unlike the bridges north of it, this one does connect to a through traffic route, that of the northern quay of the Looiersgracht. The bridge is not a monument itself.

name: Brug 66
en: Brug 66 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge is located in the extension (city exit) of the Runstraat and crosses the Prinsengracht. Unlike the bridges north of it, this bridge does connect to a continuous traffic route, namely that of the northern quay of the Looiersgracht. The bridge, itself not a monument, is surrounded by

name: Brug 69
en: Brug 69 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Spiegelgracht with the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat and crosses the Prinsengracht. The bridge is already drawn on Jacob Bosch's map of the Fourth Expansion of around 1679. In 1866 a tender was put out for a new bridge, which contractors could build for 20,000 guilders.

name: Brug 69
en: Brug 69 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge connects the Spiegelgracht with the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat and crosses the Prinsengracht. On Jacob Bosch's map with the Fourth explanation on it from around 1679, the bridge is already drawn.

name: Brug 707
en: Brug 707 is a structure in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Brug 72
en: Brug 72 and Brug 73 are two permanent bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridges are located in the banks of the Prinsengracht and cross the Reguliersgracht. Bridge 73 is on the city side (north side, odd numbers), bridge 72 on the outside side (south side, even numbers). The bridges are surrounded by municipal and national monuments.

name: Brug 73
en: Brug 72 and Brug 73 are two fixed bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum. They lie in the quays of the Prinsengracht and cross the Reguliersgracht. Bridge 73 is on the city side (north, odd numbers) and bridge 72 on the outer side (south, even numbers). Both are surrounded by municipal and national monuments.

name: Brug 73
en: Brug 72 and Brug 73 are two permanent bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridges are located in the banks of the Prinsengracht and cross the Reguliersgracht. Bridge 73 is on the city side (north side, odd numbers), bridge 72 on the outside side (south side, even numbers). The bridges are surrounded by municipal and national monuments.

name: Brug 74
en: Brug 74 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the Kerkstraat and spans the Reguliersgracht in Amsterdam's canal ring. A municipal monument since 1995, it is surrounded by national monuments, the best known of which is the Amstelkerk on the Amstelveld. A bridge has been here for centuries.

name: Brug 74
en: Brug 74 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located in Kerkstraat and spans the Reguliersgracht in the Amsterdam canal belt. The bridge, itself a municipal monument as of 1995, is surrounded by national monuments, of which the Amstelkerk on the Amstelveld is best known. There has been a bridge here for centuries.

name: Brug 75
en: Brug 75 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located in the Utrechtsestraat and crosses the Prinsengracht. It is the last bridge of the Utrechtsestraat towards the city, the once built bridge over the Achtergracht was demolished when that canal was dredged. It is the second last bridge over the Prinsengracht before it reaches the Frans Hendri

name: Brug 75
en: Brug 75 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the Utrechtsestraat and crosses the Prinsengracht. It is the last bridge of the Utrechtsestraat heading out of the city, the bridge once built over the Achtergracht having been demolished when that canal was filled in.

name: Brug 81
en: Brug 81 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located on the northern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Reguliersgracht.

name: Brug 81
en: Brug 81 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the northern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Reguliersgracht. For several centuries shipping and road traffic at this crossing of waterways were arranged so that no bridge ever lay in the western quay of the Reguliersgracht over the Lijnbaansgracht as we know it now.

name: Brug 811
en: Brug 811 is a building art work in Amsterdam-Zuid. The bridge is located in the Buitenveldertselaan and crosses a drainage ditch that ends in "Kleine Wetering"; it lands in the south on 't Kleine Loopveld. The bridge was built to create a continuous route between Amsterdam and Amstelveen, resulting in a tunnel and Brug Uilenstede. The b

name: Brug 811
en: Brug 811 is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuid. It lies in the Buitenveldertselaan and crosses a drainage channel ending in the Kleine Wetering, landing to the south on 't Kleine Loopveld. It was built to create a through route between Amsterdam and Amstelveen, continuing in a culvert and Brug Uilenstede.

name: Brug 812
en: Brug 812 is a building art work in Amsterdam-Zuid. This bridge was built around 1963 in a footpath between De Cuserstraat and Kalfjeslaan. The path crosses 't Kleine Loopveld and lies over a pond south of De Cuserstraat 3. The bridge was designed by Dirk Sterenberg of the Department of Public Works, who designed more bridges between the

name: Brug 812
en: Brug 812 is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was built around 1963 in a footpath between the De Cuserstraat and the Kalfjeslaan. The path cuts through 't Kleine Loopveld and crosses a pond south of De Cuserstraat 3. It was designed by Dirk Sterenberg of the Dienst der Publieke Werken, who designed several bridges around the Kalfjeslaan.

name: Brug 87
en: Brug 87 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the western quay of the Prinsengracht and spans the Spiegelgracht. Next to bridge 87 is bridge 69 spanning the Prinsengracht. Both bridges are surrounded by municipal and national monuments. The bridge is already drawn on the 1675 plan by Jacobus de la Feuille. The recent incident

name: Brug 87
en: Brug 87 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the western quay of the Prinsengracht and spans the Spiegelgracht. Bridge 69 lies beside it, over the Prinsengracht. Both are surrounded by municipal and national monuments. The bridge is already drawn on Jacobus de la Feuille's map of 1675.

name: Brug 89
en: Brug 89 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the Weteringstraat and spans the Lijnbaansgracht, its far end joining the Weteringpoort (bridge 90). A bridge has been here for centuries: both Daniël Stalpaert in 1662 and Frederik de Wit in 1688 drew one here on their city maps.

name: Brug 89
en: Brug 89 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located in the Weteringstraat. It spans the Lijnbaansgracht. The outlet of the bridge is connected to the Weteringpoort (bridge 90). The bridge is anachronistic. A bridge has been lying here for centuries.

name: Brug 94
en: Brug 94 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It crosses the Leidsegracht and connects the Raamdwarsstraat to the north with the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht to the south. The old building and national monument Leidsegracht 108 stands north of the bridge, and the modern Lijnbaansgracht police station to the south.

name: Brug 94
en: Brug 94 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located over the Leidsegracht and forms the connection between the Raamdwarsstraat (north) and the quay of the Lijnbaansgracht (south).

name: Brug 96
en: Brug 96 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the western quay of the Prinsengracht and crosses the Passeerdersgracht. A bridge has been here for centuries: it is already drawn on Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode's map of 1625 as a bridge over the Prince Graft and Passeerders Graft.

name: Brug 96
en: Brug 96 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the western quay of the Prinsengracht and crosses the Passeerdersgracht. There has been a bridge here for centuries. On the map of Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode from 1625, the bridge is already drawn as a bridge over the Prince Graft and Passeerders Graft.

name: Brug 97
en: Brug 97 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located on the southeastern quay of the Spiegelgracht, spans the Lijnbaansgracht and leads to the Weteringschans, locally once called Extended Spiegelgracht (but there was no canal) and Zieseniskade. Along the extension of the bridge is the Museum Bridge to the Rijksmuseum. The bridge is surrounded

name: Brug 97
en: Brug 97 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the south-eastern quay of the Spiegelgracht, spans the Lijnbaansgracht and leads to the Weteringschans, once known locally as Verlengde Spiegelgracht and Zieseniskade. The Museumbrug to the Rijksmuseum lies in line with it.

name: Brug 98
en: Brug 98 is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and crosses the Passeerdersgracht.

name: Brug 98
en: Brug 98 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and crosses the Passeerdersgracht. Since the late 18th century the Lijnbaansgracht has stopped here at the Raamplein, first called Malagplein, and only resumes at the Leidsegracht, with a culvert said to run beneath the site.

name: Brug met de twaalf gaten
en: The Brug met de twaalf gaten is a nationally protected former bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The bridge once belonged to the now almost disappeared Fort Vossegat. This fort rose around 1818 just southeast of that city in the New Holland Water Line. The bridge was built in 1862 in brick and also served as an inundation sluice.

name: Buchenwald Memorial
en: The Buchenwaldmonument is a memorial in the De Nieuwe Ooster cemetery. The monument, in the form of a gravestone, was unveiled on 26 October 1955, a week after the burial of an urn holding ashes of victims and earth from Buchenwald, Putten, Lidice, Dachau, Warsaw, Auschwitz and Oradour.

name: Buchenwald Memorial
en: The Buchenwald monument is a monument placed on De Nieuwe Ooster cemetery. The monument, in the form of a gravestone, was unveiled on October 26, 1955. A week earlier, an urn was buried in which ashes of victims and earth were stored from Buchenwald, Putten (Razzia van Putten), Lidice (slaughter), Dachau, Warsaw, Auschwitz and Orad

name: Buiksloterdraaibrug
en: The Buiksloterdraaibrug (number 2205) is a structure in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Buiksloterkanaal
en: The Buiksloterkanaal in Amsterdam-North is the connection between the (western part of the) Johan van Hasselt Canal and the IJ. The canal with north-south orientation lies between Buiksloterham in the west and Volewijck in the east. The canal was dug in 1926 in the polder Buiksloterham.

name: Buiksloterkerk
en: The Buiksloterkerk is the former village church of the dyke village of Buiksloot in Amsterdam-Noord. It does not stand along the Buiksloterdijk but slightly lower on the Buiksloterkerkpad. Rural in setting and surrounded by a graveyard, it dates from 1609 and was listed as a national monument in 1970.

name: Buiksloterkerk
en: The Buiksloterkerk is the (former) village church of the dike village Buiksloot in Amsterdam-Noord. The church building is not along the Buiksloterdijk, but slightly lower on the Buiksloterkerkpad. The church is located nationally and is surrounded by a cemetery. The building was included in the register of national monuments in 1970.

name: Buitenveldertselaan
en: The Buitenveldertselaan is a street in Amsterdam by Buitenveldert that connects the Zuid district with Amstelveen.

name: Bullebak
en: De Bullebak, bridge 149, is a double bascule bridge in Amsterdam over the Brouwersgracht, connecting the Marnixstraat with the Korte Marnixstraat at the Marnixkade. It is built of wood, steel, brick and concrete. It should not be confused with the Bullebakssluis (bridge 160), further along the Marnixstraat.

name: Bullebak
en: The Bullebak, bridge 149, is a double bascule bridge in Amsterdam over the Brouwersgracht, which connects the Marnixkade, the Marnixstraat with the Korte Marnixstraat at the level of the Marnixkade. The bridge is made of wood, steel, brick and concrete.

name: Bullebaksluis
en: The Bullebakssluis (bridge number 160) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a different bridge from De Bullebak, further along the Marnixstraat.

name: Bullewijkpadbrug
en: The Bullewijkpadbrug (bridge 1083) is a structure from 1981 in Amsterdam-Zuid. Since the Gaasperdammertunnel was built it is the only bridge still standing in the 1080-1089 series. It was designed as a viaduct by Dirk Sterenberg of the Dienst der Publieke Werken.

name: Bullewijkpadbrug
en: The Bullewijkpadbrug (bridge 1083) is a structural work of art from 1981 in Amsterdam-Zuid. It has been the only existing bridge in the series 1080-1089 since the construction of the Gaasperdammertunnel. The design for the bridge in the form of a viaduct came from Dirk Sterenberg working at the Department of Public Works.

name: Burgemeester Cramergracht
en: The Burgemeester Cramergracht is a canal and a street running parallel to it in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The canal was named in 1952 and was named after Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), mayor of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

name: Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan
en: The Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street was named in 1952 after Willem de Vlugt (1872-1945), mayor of Amsterdam from 1921 to 1941, when he was removed from office after the February Strike.

name: Burgemeester Eliasstraat
en: The Burgemeester Eliasstraat is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, located in the Slotermeer Zuid neighborhood. The Burgemeester Eliasstraat is located between the Haarlemmerweg and the Louis Couperusstraat in Slotermeer. The street is crossed by the Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan, the Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan and the Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht.

name: Burgemeester Fockstraat
en: The Burgemeester Fockstraat is a street in Slotermeer, Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street was named on July 9, 1952 and was named after Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), mayor of Amsterdam from 1866 to 1868, then Commissioner of the King for South Holland. Several streets in the district were named after Amsterdam mayors.

name: Burgemeester Hogguerstraat
en: The Burgemeester Hogguerstraat is a street in Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street begins at Burgemeester Van de Pollstraat and runs to Burgemeester Rendorpstraat. The street was named in 1958 and was named after Mr. Paul Iwan Hogguer (1760-1816), mayor of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1816. The street is dominated by three in

name: Burgemeester Norbruislaan
en: The Burgemeester Norbruislaan is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht.

name: Burgemeester Röellstraat
en: The Burgemeester Röellstraat is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street runs from the Jan van Galenstraat metro station and lies along the extension of Jan van Galenstraat. The street then runs in a westerly direction to Lambertus Zijlplein. The surname Röell is pronounced as Reu-el, so the stress is on the letter o. A common

name: Burgemeester Stramanweg
en: The Burgemeester Stramanweg is an important main road in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel and the municipality of Amsterdam, Zuidoost district.

name: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht
en: The Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht in Amsterdam Nieuw-West was built in the 1950s as part of the Western Garden Cities. The canal is located in Slotermeer and is the extension of the Erasmusgracht. The canal ends in a bend at the Plein '40-'45. The canal was named in 1952 and was named after Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), bu

name: Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan
en: The Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan is located in the district ("garden city") Slotermeer in the Amsterdam municipality of Nieuw-West.

name: Camera Obscurabrug
en: The Camera Obscurabrug (bridge 322) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies in line with the Leeuwendalersweg to the south and spans the Erasmusgracht, which west of the bridge takes the name Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht. The bridge dates from 1961/1962.

name: Camera Obscurabrug
en: The Camera Obscurabrug (bridge 322) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is located in the extension of the Leeuwendalersweg southwards. It spans the Erasmusgracht, which west of the bridge is named Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht.

name: Carel Willinkplantsoen
en: The Carel Willinkplantsoen is a relatively small park in Amsterdam.

name: Caroline Herschelbrug
en: Caroline Herschelbrug (bridge 115) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. This pedestrian bridge connects Celebesstraat with the Ooster Ringdijk and spans the ring canal of Watergraafsmeer. A bridge with a budget of 5500 guilders was built there in 1927. The bridge was designed at the time by Piet Kramer of the Department of Public Works.

name: Caroline Herschelbrug
en: Caroline Herschelbrug (bridge 115) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. This footbridge connects the Celebesstraat with the Ooster Ringdijk, spanning the ring canal of the Watergraafsmeer. A bridge was built here in 1927 with a budget of 5,500 guilders, designed by Piet Kramer of the Dienst der Publieke Werken.

name: Cecilia van Alphen-Jagtmanbrug
en: The Cecilia van Alphen-Jagtmanbrug (bridge 912) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. It connects the Buiksloterdijk to the west with a T-junction to the east. Between house numbers 240-242, a municipal monument, and 248, the Buiksloterdijk has a side road running north-east to that junction.

name: Cecilia van Alphen-Jagtmanbrug
en: The Cecilia van Alphen-Jagtmanbrug (bridge 912) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-North. It forms the connection between the western Buiksloterdijk and a T-intersection on the eastern side. The Buiksloterdijk has a side road here between house numbers 240-242 (a municipal monument) and 248, which runs northeast. At that T-intersection, the Nieuwe Purmer

name: Ceintuurbrug
en: The Ceintuurbrug (bridge no. 116) is a slab bridge over the Boerenwetering in Amsterdam-Zuid. It connects the Ceintuurbaan with the Roelof Hartstraat and forms part of the ring of streets just outside the inner-city ring. It should not be confused with the Nieuwe Amstelbrug (bridge no. 101) at the other end of the Ceintuurbaan.

name: Ceintuurbrug
en: The Ceintuurbrug (bridge no. 116) is a plate bridge over the Boerenwetering in Amsterdam-Zuid. The bridge connects the Ceintuurbaan with the Roelof Hartstraat and is part of the ring of streets that lie just outside the inner city ring.

name: Charley Tooropbrug
en: The Charley Tooropbrug (bridge 656) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies in the Postjesweg and spans a ditch running parallel to the Ringspoorbaan and metro line 50. The Postjesweg becomes the Robert Fruinlaan here. There is a ditch on the far side of the railway too, but it is not bridged.

name: Charley Tooropbrug
en: The Charley Tooropbrug (bridge 656) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The bridge is located on Postjesweg and spans a ditch that runs parallel to the Ringspoorbaan and metro line 50 there. Postjesweg transitions into Robert Fruinlaan here. On the other side of the Ringspoorlijn there is also a ditch but there is no bridge over it. Directly at the

name: Chinatown
en: Chinatown is the Chinese quarter of Amsterdam. It lies around the Geldersekade and the Zeedijk in the old inner city, Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
en: The Christoffel Plantijnpad (and the Christoffel Plantijngracht) in Amsterdam-Slotervaart have been named after the South Dutch printer and lexicographer Christoffel Plantijn (1514-1589), who owned a famous printing house and publishing house in Antwerp. The 3 kilometer long path forms the western boundary of the garden city Slotervaart and begins at

name: Church of England
en: Christ Church in Amsterdam is a former cloth hall on the Groenburgwal converted into an Anglican church. It is one of the first, possibly the first, buildings in the Netherlands in the neo-Gothic manner. It was entered in the monuments register on 28 April 1970.

name: Churchilllaan
en: Churchilllaan is a street in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. Until May 1946 it was called Noorder Amstellaan.

name: Cinecenter
en: Cinecenter is an Amsterdam cinema in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located at Lijnbaansgracht 236 near Leidseplein. The cinema or film house was in 1979 the continuation of the CinéTol cinema, which was closed approximately at the same time by Cor Koppies. That came into conflict with the municipality of Amsterdam, which first wants the complex on Tolstraat

name: Coenhaven
en: The Coenhaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area north of the Vlothaven, south of the North Sea Canal near the Coentunnel named after the port, east of the Petroleum Port and west of the Mercuriushaven. The port has provided space for ships and activities that are no longer desired in the Eastern Port Area

name: Colignybrug
en: The Colignybrug is a monumental bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. It spans the Minstroom and forms a connection between Louise de Colignystraat and Hobbemastraat. It is a fixed bridge with limited clearance height. The materials used are iron/steel, natural stone and brick. The Colignybrug is a municipal monument. The bridge dates back to

name: Collectie Six
en: The Collectie Six is the collective name for the heritage of the Six family, which besides the family portraits includes the family archive and works of art and antiques connected with the family. The Six Stichting, the Stichting Stella Duce, the Jan Six Stichting founded in 2010 and Stichting Amstel 218 together make up the collection.

name: Collectie Six
en: The Collectie Six is the common name for the patrimony of the Six family that, in addition to the family portraits, includes the family archive and art and antique objects related to the family, among other things.

name: Commandantsbrug
en: Commandantsbrug is the unofficial name of structure bridge 2361 in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Compagnietheater
en: The Compagnietheater is housed in the former church of the Reformed Lutheran church on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam.

name: Constantiahofje
en: Constantia is a residential complex around a green courtyard on Willemsstraat 149-165 in Amsterdam, which was built in neoclassical style in 1863. The 36 houses were designed by architect Pieter Johannes Hamer on behalf of the 'Stichting voor den Ambachtsstand - Constantia Woningen'. The houses were (free of rent) intended for workers

name: Cornelis Lelylaan
en: The Cornelis Lelylaan is a city motorway in Amsterdam (part of the city route s106) that connects the districts West and Nieuw-West. The Amsterdam Lelylaan train and metro station is located across the road and is named after it. On the site of the road was originally the Slotervaart which was drowned and disappeared under the sand.

name: Corry Tendeloobrug
en: The Corry Tendeloobrug (bridge 713) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The bridge is located on Johan Huizingalaan and spans a canal that runs parallel to Aletta Jacobslaan and Louwesweg on the north side. Aletta Jacobslaan becomes Louwesweg at the intersection with Johan Huizingalaan. The bridge was built during a period when the terrain

name: Corry Tendeloobrug
en: The Corry Tendeloobrug (bridge 713) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies in the Johan Huizingalaan and spans a canal running parallel to the Aletta Jacobslaan and Louwesweg on the north side. At the crossing with the Johan Huizingalaan the Aletta Jacobslaan becomes the Louwesweg.

name: Croeselaan
en: The Croeselaan is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht. It runs from Westplein to Vondellaan and lies between Utrecht Central Station and the Jaarbeurs.

name: Da Costagracht
en: The Da Costagracht is a canal in Amsterdam-West. The canal connects the Hugo de Grootgracht in the north with the Jacob van Lennepkanaal in the south. The canal is named after the 19th-century poet and prose writer Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860).

name: Daalseweg
en: Daalseweg can refer to: Daalseweg - the Zuilense name of the Daalsedijk Daalseweg - a road in Nijmegen-Oost

name: Daalwijkdreef
en: The Daalwijkdreef is a promenade in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The first part of the elevated promenade, exclusively for fast traffic, was opened in 1971. The promenade connects the Dolingadreef in the west of the Bijlmermeer with the Elsrijkdreef in the east where the promenade turns right at a bend. Originally, the promenade began at the m

name: Dafne Schippersbrug
en: The Dafne Schippersbrug is a bicycle and pedestrian bridge over the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal in Utrecht. This bridge is located on the shortest cycling route between Utrecht City Center on the east side and the geographical center of the Utrecht district of Leidsche Rijn and the hometown of De Meern on the west side.

name: Dageraadsbrug
en: The Dageraadsbrug (bridge 353) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Dam Square Victims 7 mei 1945
en: A plaque and thirty-two street stones on the Dam in Amsterdam-Centrum commemorate the victims of the Shooting on the Dam on May 7, 1945.

name: Dam Square Victims 7 mei 1945
en: A plaque and thirty-two paving stones on the Dam in Amsterdam-Centrum commemorate the victims of the shooting on the Dam on 7 May 1945.

name: Darwinplantsoen
en: Darwinplantsoen is a street and a park in the Dutch capital Amsterdam, more specifically in Amsterdam-Oost, Watergraafsmeer.

name: David van Mollembrug
en: The David van Mollembrug is a bascule bridge over the Vecht River in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The bridge was opened in 1965 and forms a connection between David van Mollemstraat and the Draaiweg. The bridge is named after silk merchant David van Mollem (1670-1746), who had his country house Zijdebalen here.

name: De Alpen
en: De Alpen is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street was named on October 20, 1993, but was finally determined on September 24, 1997. It was named after the Alpine mountain range. Looking from the center of Amsterdam, De Alpen begins at Ecuplein with the Lirabrug (bridge 1883) over a ring canal. Then it goes one kilometer in a straight line

name: De Ark
en: De Ark is a church building in the Slotervaart district in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The church was built in 1960-'61 according to the design of architect Piet Zanstra. The building has been on the municipal monument list since 2008 and on the Top-100 of young monuments of Amsterdam.

name: De Boelelaan
en: The De Boelelaan in Amsterdam-Buitenveldert was named on January 15, 1958 and was named after Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

name: De Dokwerker
en: De Dokwerker is a statue and monument on the Jonas Daniël Meijerplein in Amsterdam commemorating the February Strike of 1941. It was designed and made by the sculptor Mari Andriessen on the commission of the Amsterdam city council. The Haarlem carpenter and contractor Willem Termetz, who knew Andriessen before the war, modelled for it in 1951.

name: De Dokwerker
en: De Dokwerker is a statue and monument on Jonas Daniël Meijerplein in Amsterdam in memory of the February Strike of 1941. The statue was designed and made by the sculptor Mari Andriessen on commission of the Amsterdam municipal government. The Haarlem carpenter/contractor Willem Termetz, who already knew Andriessen before the war, in 1951

name: De Dolphijn
en: The house De Dolphijn is a canal house at Singel 140-142 in Amsterdam. Its best-known resident was Frans Banninck Cocq, who lived there when Rembrandt painted Cocq's militia company between 1640 and 1642, in the painting now known as The Night Watch.

name: De Duifbrug
en: De Duifbrug, Duyfjesbrug or Duyfjessluis is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located on the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht across the Prinsengracht.

name: De Duifbrug
en: De Duifbrug, also Duyfjesbrug or Duyfjessluis, is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht over the Prinsengracht. On the south side of the Prinsengracht here the whole frontage consists of municipal and national monuments, the best known being the 1857 church De Duif, after which the bridge is named.

name: De Gesloten Steen
en: De Gesloten Steen (also known as devil's stone) is a heavy stray stone in the center of Utrecht. The national monument stone is chained to the corner of Oudegracht and the Eligenhof on a corner building that has taken its name from it.

name: De Groene Kop
en: Park De Groene Kop is a park on the north side of Tuindorp Oost, a neighborhood in the Noordoost district in Utrecht. The park is located between the Eykmanlaan, Winklerlaan, the community garden park de Driehoek and the Utrecht-Amersfoort railway line.

name: De Hallen
en: The Hallen is a cultural center in the Kinkerbuurt in Amsterdam-West, with more than two million visitors per year. It houses the Filmhallen, FoodHallen, De Hallen Studios, Kanarie Club, Hal West, various shops, a hotel, a daycare center, the Beeldend Gesproken gallery and a branch of the Openbare Bibliotheek Amsterdam with reading café Belcampo. name: De Hallen
en: De Hallen is a cultural centre in the Kinkerbuurt in Amsterdam-West with more than two million visitors a year. It houses the Filmhallen, FoodHallen, De Hallen Studio's, Kanarie Club, Hal West, various shops, a hotel, a nursery, the gallery Beeldend Gesproken and a branch of the Amsterdam public library.

name: De hongerwinter
en: De hongerwinter is a war memorial on the Eastern Islands in Amsterdam-Centrum, concerning the famine winter of 1944/1945. It exists in two versions. The original, by Hildo Krop, is placed in the Oosterkerk; it was first mounted on the street side but was eaten away over the years by weather and soot.

name: De hongerwinter
en: De hongerwinter is a war monument on the Eastern Islands in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is about the hunger winter of 1944/1945. It exists in two versions: The original, by Hildo Krop, is located in the Oosterkerk. This was first installed on the street side, but over the years has been eaten away by weather influences and rust. The i

name: De Inktpot
en: De Inktpot is the largest brick building in the Netherlands, designed by George van Heukelom on behalf of the public interest association Dutch Railways (NS). The national monument is located in Moreelsepark in Utrecht near Utrecht Central Station and has been used since 1995 as the headquarters of ProRail.

name: De Inktpot
en: De Inktpot is the largest brick building in the Netherlands, designed by George van Heukelom on behalf of the public interest association Dutch Railways (NS). The national monument is located in Moreelsepark in Utrecht near Utrecht Central Station and has been used since 1995 as the headquarters of ProRail.

name: De Knoop
en: De knoop is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Noord. The name, in use for many years, refers to an originally untitled work by André Volten. The sculpture, several metres high, works out an essentially simple idea: it is a boundary marker and at the same time a link between Amsterdam-Noord and the IJ, two intertwined links standing on two supports.

name: De Kom
en: De Kom is an unofficial name for a body of water in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is a crossroads of five waterways. These waterways also have a bridge on "De Kom" except for one.

name: De Krakeling
en: De Krakeling is a theater hall in Amsterdam focused on youth theater. De Krakeling was founded in 1978 by Hans Snoek. It was the first theater building in the Netherlands specially designed for youth theater. The name "De Krakeling" was a reference to the adjacent Koekjesbrug in the Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat. The theater is part of the founded in 1971

name: De Krommert
en: De Krommert (also known as De Krommerdt) is a neighborhood in the Amsterdam district of West, named after the De Krommert waterway.

name: De Meernbrug
en: The De Meernbrug, not to be confused with the Meern Bridge (without article De) in the center of De Meern, is a arched bridge over the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal near the Utrecht Jaarbeurs and not far from De Meern.

name: De Nieuwe Stad
en: Kerkcentrum De Nieuwe Stad is a church in Amsterdam-Zuidoost (Bijlmermeer), built in 1992/1993 and designed by the architects Lafour and Wijk.

name: De Rijpgracht
en: The De Rijpgracht is a canal in the Amsterdam neighborhood of Landlust. The canal was named after the explorer Jan Corneliszoon Rijp (1570-1630) by a council decision of April 27, 1933, with the understanding that the canal and associated street have an article (the De Rijpgracht).

name: De Ruijterkade
en: The De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam is located along the IJ on the north side of Central Station. The quay was built in 1880 on the new Station Island, as part of a restructuring project of the traffic flows, in connection with the construction of the North Sea Canal and the expansions of train traffic. The De Ruijterkade is named after Michiel Adria

name: De Tol
en: De Tol can refer to: De Tol (Sluis), a hamlet in the Dutch municipality of Sluis De Tol, monumental farm and former castle in the Dutch village of Koudekerk Het Sluisje (Rhoon), a vanished hamlet in Rhoon, also known as De Tol

name: De Vriendschap
en: De Vriendschap is a windmill built in 1900 on the site of a mill that burned down in 1899. It stands at Utrechtseweg 11a on the Utrechtse Vecht in Weesp.

name: De Vrouwenbibliotheek
en: De Vrouwenbibliotheek and Documentatiecentrum Utrecht (VDU), founded in 1984, was a place where women in the Dutch city of Utrecht and its surroundings could find feminist literature, documentary material and non-fiction about women's culture, and where they also had a meeting place. De Vrouwenbibliotheek was thus part of the women's movement

name: Demka-spoorbrug
en: The Demka-spoorbrug is a railway bridge over the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal in Utrecht. The bridge is a steel reinforced beam arch bridge and was built in 1966 to replace the old, much smaller railway bridge that had to disappear due to the widening of the canal. The span is 173 meters. The bridge is named after the nearby former steelworks

name: Dick Schmüllbrug
en: Dick Schmüllbrug (bridge 415) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid. The traffic bridge, also carrying GVB bus 15, lies in the Parnassusweg and spans the Zuider Amstelkanaal. The Stadionkade runs along it to the north and the Locatellikade and Henri Viottakade to the south. It was designed in the Amsterdam School style.

name: Dick Schmüllbrug
en: Dick Schmüllbrug (bridge 415) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid. The traffic bridge, over which GVB bus 15 also runs, is located on Parnassusweg and spans the Zuider Amstel Canal. In the north, the Stadionkade runs along the bridge and in the south the Locatellikade and Henri Viottakade.

name: Diepenbrockstraat
en: The Diepenbrockstraat is a street in Amsterdam - Zuid. The street runs along the Wielingenstraat, which runs along the RAI exhibition center. The street begins on Bridge 422 over the Boerenwetering, from there the street runs in a circular shape over a bridge over the Zuider Amstel Canal. The street ends on the Stadionweg. The street was on September 30

name: Dirk de Waterduikerbrug
en: The Dirk de Waterduikerbrug (bridge 617) is a fixed bridge in the Slotermeer district in the Amsterdam Nieuw-West district. The bridge is located in the Noordzijde street and crosses a culvert, which connects the water of the marina on the north side of the Sloterplas with a narrow canal that runs in a northerly direction.

name: Dirk de Waterduikerbrug
en: The Dirk de Waterduikerbrug (bridge 617) is a fixed bridge in the Slotermeer district of Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It lies in the street Noordzijde and crosses a culvert connecting the water of the marina on the north side of the Sloterplas with a narrow canal running north.

name: Doelensluis
en: The Doelensluis (bridge 220) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Dolingadreef
en: The Dolingadreef is a dike in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

name: Domela Nieuwenhuisplantsoen
en: The Domela Nieuwenhuisplantsoen is a small garden in the shape of a triangle in the Spaarndammerbuurt neighborhood in Amsterdam-West.

name: Dominicuskerk
en: The Dominicuskerk is a neo-Gothic church building on Spuistraat in Amsterdam. It was built as a Roman Catholic Parish Church of St. Dominic by Pierre Cuypers and served by the Dominicans. The church is no longer part of the Catholic Church, but is used by the Dominican community and rented out.

name: Domplein
en: The Domplein is a square in the city center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. It is named after the Dom Church, which is located on the square.

name: Doopsgezinde kerk
en: The Doopsgezinde kerk "Vermaning" in the Dutch city of Utrecht is located on the Oudegracht. It was established in 1773 by a thorough renovation of a medieval canal house under the leadership of the Haarlem architect Willem de Haan. Until then, the Baptists had used a building on Springweg. The new front facade on the Oudegra

name: Dorpskerk Durgerdam
en: The Dorpskerk Durgerdam, originally the Reformed church of Durgerdam, is the Protestant church of Durgerdam in Amsterdam-Noord. It does not stand along the Durgerdammerdijk but slightly lower behind it. Its congregation belongs to the Protestant Church in the Netherlands.

name: Dr. Samuel de Ranitzbrug
en: The Dr. Samuel de Ranitzbrug (bridge no. 187), also known as the Spinozabrug, is a former railway bridge over the Singelgracht in Amsterdam, between the Mauritskade and the Spinozastraat. The city of Amsterdam also refers to it as bridge 187. It is part of the waterway between the Open Havenfront and the Amstel.

name: Dr. Samuel de Ranitzbrug
en: The Dr. Samuel de Ranitzbrug (bridge no. 187), also known as the Spinoza Bridge, is a former railway bridge over the Singelgracht in Amsterdam, between the Mauritskade and the Spinozastraat. The Municipality of Amsterdam also refers to the bridge as bridge 187. The bridge is part of the waterway between the Open Havenfront and the Amstel.

name: Drieharingenbrug
en: The Drieharingenbrug (bridge 320) is a double lift bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge forms the connection between the Realeneiland and the Prinseneiland and spans the Realengracht. It lies southwards along the extension of the Vierwindendwarsstraat and leads to the Prinseneiland street. East of the bridge is the Zandhoeksbrug with the same appearance

name: Drieharingenbrug
en: The Drieharingenbrug (bridge 320) is a double drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects Realeneiland with Prinseneiland, spanning the Realengracht. It lies south in line with the Vierwindendwarsstraat and leads to the street Prinseneiland. The identical-looking Zandhoeksbrug lies to its east.

name: Drift
en: The Drift is a canal and street in the city center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. It connects to the Kromme Nieuwegracht in the south and continues into the Plompetorengracht in the north. Today it is crossed by the continuous road/busway over the Janskerkhof and Nobelstraat; however, in the past the Drift was as a traffic artery of more b

name: Driftbrug
en: The Driftbrug is a fixed bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. It is located in the northeast of the city center. The bridge spans the Drift which at this point flows into the Plompetorengracht. By land, the Driftbrug connects the Voorstraat with the Wittevrouwenstraat.

name: Drs. P-brug
en: The Drs. P-brug (bridge 2115) is a structure in Amsterdam-Noord. Its working name was the Ridderspoorbrug.

name: Duivendrechtsevaart
en: The Duivendrechtsevaart is a canal in Amsterdam and Duivendrecht (Ouder-Amstel municipality). The waterway runs from the Amstel near the Omval to the Van der Madeweg in the Overamstel industrial area. The municipal border between Amsterdam and Ouder-Amstel runs across the canal. The waterway is named after the nearby village of Duivendrecht.

name: Duizendste Brug
en: The Duizendste brug (bridge 684) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It spans the Postjeswetering, connecting the Antillenstraat in the Surinamebuurt with the Rembrandtpark. It is the larger sister of bridges 682 and 683, and by that analogy also a daughter of the Torontobrug.

name: Dutch National Opera & Ballet
en: Nationale Opera & Ballet, formerly Het Muziektheater Amsterdam, is a theatre in Amsterdam built specially for staging operas, ballets and other forms of music theatre. It is also the name of the organisation that, besides the theatre, comprises the companies De Nationale Opera and Het Nationale Ballet.

name: Dutch National Opera & Ballet
en: National Opera & Ballet (formerly Het Muziektheater Amsterdam) is a theater in Amsterdam that was specially built for the performance of operas, ballets and other forms of music theater. It is also the name of the organization that includes the companies De Nationale Opera and Het Nationale Ballet in addition to the theater. The theater is part of he

name: Ecuplein
en: The Ecuplein is a square in the De Aker district in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It is located at the end of Pieter Calandlaan. The square was named in 1997 after the 'European Currency Unit' (ECU), the financial unit of account of the European Community, which was replaced by the euro on January 1, 1999.

name: Eén Honderd Roedebrug
en: Brug 347 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West.

name: Eendrachtspark
en: The Eendrachtspark is a city park in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Elsje Christiaensbrug
en: The Elsje Christiaensbrug (bridge 2474) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-North. The traffic bridge is located over the Buiksloterkanaal and is located on Tolhuisweg.

name: Elsje Christiaensbrug
en: The Elsje Christiaensbrug (bridge 2474) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. The traffic bridge crosses the Buiksloterkanaal and lies in the Tolhuisweg, which in the 21st century grew into a traffic route between the Van der Pekbuurt, a relatively old residential area, and the newer Overhoeksbuurt.

name: Elthetokerk
en: The former Elthetokerk was a Reformed church building at the corner of Insulindeweg and Kramatweg in the Indische Buurt in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Entrepothaven
en: The Entrepothaven in Amsterdam is a trumpet-shaped body of water in the Eastern Harbor Area of Amsterdam. The harbor was built in 1898-1900 and is 1.2 km long, maximum 200 meters wide but tapering to the west. The depth is measured between 5 and 7 meters. It is the most eastern harbor of Amsterdam and stretches from the Amsterdam-Rhineka

name: Erasmusgracht
en: The Erasmusgracht in Amsterdam-West was built in the 1940s as part of the new Bos en Lommer district. Along the extension beyond the dike of the Ringspoorbaan lies the Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht. The canal was named in 1939 and was named after Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), famous Dutch humanist. The canal runs from the Admiral

name: Erasmuspark
en: The Erasmuspark is a city park in Amsterdam-West. It is also the name of the neighborhood in which it is located.

name: Ertshaven
en: The Ertshaven is a port in the Eastern Port Area of Amsterdam. The port is located east of the Connecting Dam, with the Blauwehoofdbrug in it, and flows into the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.

name: Esperantomonument
en: Esperanto monuments in the Netherlands were established in honor of the Esperanto language and/or the creator of that language, Lejzer Zamenhof. In the Netherlands there are six of these types of monuments: in the towns of Bergen op Zoom, Den Burg, Leeuwarden, Utrecht and Zwolle.

name: Etty Hillesumbrug
en: The Etty Hillesumbrug (bridge 409) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Europaboulevard
en: The Europaboulevard is a street in Buitenveldert in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Europaboulevard was named after the continent of Europe on July 16, 1958 following a resolution of the Advisory Assembly of the Council of Europe of December 29, 1957, in which every municipality in Europe was asked to name a street or square after it. The part that is in Bu

name: Europaplein
en: The Europaplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Europaplein metro station is named after it. The square consists of a traffic road and the area in front of the RAI complex. The other side of the road is also called Europaplein and on the site of the former tram loop is a small park.

name: Eva Schalkbrug
en: The Eva Schalkbrug (bridge 997) is a fixed bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in Amsterdam-Noord. It lies in the Noorderpark and spans both part of the park and the Noord-Hollandsch Kanaal. The whole area was reshaped in the 2000s and 2010s by the construction of the Noord-Zuidlijn, when the Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was lowered.

name: Eva Schalkbrug
en: The Eva Schalkbrug (bridge 997) is a permanent bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in Amsterdam-Noord. It is located in Noorderpark and spans both part of the park and the North Holland Canal. In the years zero and ten of the 21st century, as a result of the construction of the North-South Line, the entire surrounding area here was adapted.

name: Exbunker
en: The bunker in Wilhelminapark was built in 1943 as a bombproof German personnel bunker in Wilhelminapark in Utrecht. After 1945, the bunker was mainly a hindrance. Due to its cultural historical value, it has been a municipal monument since 2001 and has been used since 2014 by visual artists as an exhibition space.

name: Ezelsbrug
en: The Ezelsbrug (bridge no. 1904) is a structure in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Faralda NDSM Crane Hotel Amsterdam
en: The Crane Hotel Faralda (Kraanhotel Faralda) is a hotel located on top of a Rijksmonumentale crane on the NDSM site, a former shipyard on the banks of the IJ in Amsterdam-North. The former NDSM crane (number 13) was built in the 1950s by the firm Hensen. After 1984, the crane was dismantled after the bankruptcy of the "Nederlandsche Dok e

name: Faralda NDSM Crane Hotel Amsterdam
en: The Crane Hotel Faralda is a hotel housed at the top of a listed crane on the NDSM site, a former shipyard on the banks of the IJ in Amsterdam-Noord. The former NDSM crane, number 13, was built in the 1950s by the Hensen firm, and was left after the shipbuilder went bankrupt in 1984.

name: Fatih
en: The Fatih mosque is a mosque on the Rozengracht in the Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum. It is located in the former Roman Catholic St. Ignatius Church, also known as De Zaaier.

name: Filmhallen
en: The Filmhallen, also known as FilmHallen, is a movie theater in the De Hallen complex in the former tram depot Tollensstraat in Amsterdam-West. The operators are Kadir Selçuk and Alex Rutten of The Movies. The cinema has been open since September 4, 2014, with the premiere of the Dutch feature film Nena by Saskia Diesing on September 8.

name: Filmhuis Cavia
en: Filmhuis Cavia is a film theater in the Van Hallstraat in the Amsterdam Staatsliedenbuurt that is run entirely by volunteers. The cinema emerged in the 1980s from the squatting movement and has a simple formula: it shows what cannot be seen elsewhere. Filmhuis Cavia is located in the former Prinses Beatrix Schipp

name: Fort aan de Klop
en: Fort aan de Klop is a defensive work on the Vecht River in Utrecht. The fort was built in 1819. The function of the fort consisted, among other things, of protecting the city of Utrecht. It was also part of the New Holland Water Line.

name: Fort bij Rijnauwen
en: Fort bij Rijnauwen is a Dutch fort near the hamlet of Rhijnauwen in the municipality of Bunnik. It is part of the Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie (NHW).

name: Fort bij Uitermeer
en: Fort Uitermeer is an old fort that formed part of the New Dutch Waterline and later the Defence Line of Amsterdam. It lies in the North Holland municipality of Weesp on the east bank of the Vecht, south-east of Weesp near the hamlet of Uitermeer, with Fort bij Hinderdam to the south-west and the Weesp fortress to the north-west.

name: Fort bij Uitermeer
en: Fort Uitermeer is an old fort that was included in the New Holland Water Line and later the Stelling of Amsterdam. It is located in the North Holland municipality of Weesp on the eastern bank of the Vecht, southeast of Weesp near the hamlet of Uitermeer. To the southwest is the Fort at Hinderdam and to the northwest is the Weesp Fortress.

name: Fort Blauwkapel
en: Fort Blauwkapel (also known as: Blaucapel) is a Dutch fort near Utrecht. The fort was built in 1818-1821 as part of the Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie and is one of the largest forts of the line. Blauwkapel is a protected cityscape.

name: Fort de Bilt
